body: English has many words for sights and sounds, but it is surprisingly poor at naming smells — we often borrow words from other senses, saying something "smells sweet" or "smells like" something else.
英语里有大量形容视觉和听觉的词，却惊人地匮乏描写气味的词汇——我们常借用其他感官的说法，比如"闻起来甜甜的"或"闻起来像某样东西"。
In the programme, Neil and Georgie talk about why this gap exists and share their own favourite and worst smells, showing how personal and cultural smell memories can be.
节目里 Neil 和 Georgie 聊到这种空缺为何存在，并分享了自己最喜欢和最讨厌的气味，说明气味记忆有多私人、多受文化影响。
They also teach useful vocabulary for discussing scents, reminding learners that describing a smell well is a real skill worth practising in daily conversation.
他们还教了描述气味的好用词汇，提醒学习者：把气味说清楚，是日常对话里值得练习的真本事。
tips: 闻起来香甜（借味觉形容气味）
闻起来像……（用他物类比气味）
气味记忆（由气味触发的回忆）

body: "Gatekeep" started online as a word for controlling who gets into a group or sees certain information, like a gatekeeper at a door.
"Gatekeep" 最初是网络用语，指控制谁能进某个圈子、谁看得到某些信息，像门口的看门人。
Now people also use it to describe someone who refuses to share knowledge on purpose — for example, not telling friends about a great café so it stays quiet.
现在也常用来形容有人故意不分享知识，比如不告诉朋友一家很棒的咖啡馆，好让它一直冷清。
The speakers explain that gatekeeping can be playful, but it sometimes stops others from learning or joining in.
节目讲解道，把信息捂着有时只是开玩笑，但有时也会阻碍别人学习或参与。
tips: 把某事藏在自己心里不告诉别人

body: "Wrap it up" can mean to finish a task or bring a project to a close, like wrapping a gift when you are done.
"Wrap it up" 可以指把任务做完、给项目收尾，就像礼物包好就完成了。
It is also used when someone wants others to stop talking or stop an activity that has gone on too long.
它也用于想让别人打住、别再没完没了地说或做的时候。
The programme gives everyday examples so learners can use the phrase both at work and in casual chat.
节目给出生活化例子，方便学习者在职场和闲聊里都能用上这句话。

articles.zh: Throw ideas at the wall（把点子往上扔，看哪个粘住）
body: This phrase means to suggest many ideas quickly without judging them, just to see which ones might work.
这个短语意思是快速抛出很多点子、先不评判，看哪个能行。
The image is of throwing things at a wall to see what sticks — some fall, but a few stay.
画面感就像把东西往墙上扔，看什么能粘住——有的掉下来，但总有少数留下。
It is common in brainstorming, where the goal is quantity first and quality later.
这常见于头脑风暴，目标是先求数量、后求质量。
tips: 没有坏点子（先发散后收敛）

articles.zh: 和 hand（手）有关的四个短语
body: Georgie introduces four common English phrases built around the word "hand", showing how this body part shapes our language about control and help.
Georgie 介绍了四个围绕 hand（手）的常用短语，展现这个身体部位如何塑造我们关于"掌控"和"帮忙"的表达。
"In good hands" means something is being looked after properly, while "out of hand" describes a situation that has lost control.
"In good hands" 表示被妥善照管，而 "out of hand" 形容局面失控。
The other two — "hands down" (without doubt) and "give a hand" (to help) — are handy for daily chat and polite requests.
另外两个——"hands down"（毫无疑问）和 "give a hand"（搭把手帮忙）——在日常闲聊和礼貌请求里都很好用。
tips: 被妥善照管/由专业人士处理
